content: Quinine sulfate is contraindicated in patients with the following conditions: 1. Prolonged QT interval: Administration of quinine sulfate is contraindicated in patients with a prolonged QT interval. A fatal case of ventricular arrhythmia was reported in an elderly patient with a baseline prolonged QT interval who received intravenous quinine sulfate for the treatment of Plasmodium falciparum malaria. 2. Glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) deficiency: Patients with G6PD deficiency are at risk of hemolysis when treated with quinine. 3. Known hypersensitivity reactions to quinine: Hypersensitivity reactions to quinine may include, but are not limited to: Thrombocytopenia Idiopathic thrombocytopenic purpura (ITP) Thrombotic thrombocytopenic purpura (TTP) Hemolytic uremic syndrome (HUS) Blackwater fever, which is characterized by acute intravascular hemolysis, hemoglobinuria, and hemoglobinemia. 4. Known hypersensitivity to mefloquine or quinidine: Cross-sensitivity to quinine has been documented in patients with hypersensitivity to these agents. 5. Myasthenia gravis: Quinine has neuromuscular blocking activity and may worsen muscle weakness in patients with myasthenia gravis. 6. Optic neuritis: Quinine may exacerbate active optic neuritis and is therefore contraindicated in such cases.
